questions.stem: The angle at the centre of a circle is $140°$. What is the angle at the circumference subtended by the same arc?
questions.explanation: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference when both are subtended by the same arc. So the angle at the circumference is $\frac{140°}{2} = 70°$.

questions.stem: An angle in a semicircle (subtended by a diameter) is always:
questions.explanation: The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference is always $90°$. This is because the angle at the centre is $180°$ (a straight line), and the angle at the circumference is half of that.
